# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @9bea0f9052e877a0dd44149aaaa92d31e114d6c0 — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@b93dc51c1030839153c9bb86c8aa2e6b3fad82de
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot

# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:

    types: [completed]

  pull-requests: write

    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# The dev→review→rewor…

blocks.text:
# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
#       secrets: inherit

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      factory_ref:
        description: 'The dmtools-agents ref the factory runs from (the literal in the stub uses-line). github.workflow_ref cannot serve: in a called workflow it carries the CALLER ref, not the uses-ref.'
        required: true
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" skips — for pure-Dart targets that only need dart from the runner image. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0").'
        required: false
        default: 'stable'
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  # actions/cache@v6 save phase needs actions:write on github.token.
  actions: write

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      config: ${{ steps.check.outputs.config }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
      anchor: ${{ steps.check.outputs.anchor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository (config, runners)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # caller-repo checkout: the factory reads .dmtools/config.js from
          # the TARGET repository, never from the factory pack
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          # Event context rides through from the caller (issues events) —
          # empty for pure dispatches. The guard ALWAYS refreshes from the
          # API (queued runs see a stale payload); this is only a fallback.
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.action || github.event_name }}
          # #544: the `labeled` event sender — the owner-override gate checks
          # its repo permission before honoring a manual agent:rework.
          # Empty for schedule-scan dispatches (SM ticks): the label is
          # trusted as-is there (see rework_override_ok below).

# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home. GitHub requires reusable workflows at the
# .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the callee
# does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing declared one fails
# the guard test (factory_stub_ref_test.dart parity in each caller).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: "PAT for GitHub tool calls + gh CLI (SM engine + validation probes)."
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "Optional dedicated silent-update token; the silent-token input wins when both are set."
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

env:
  # Version knobs resolve from the CALLER's repository variables (vars.*
  # resolve in the caller's context for reusable workflows) — bumping an
  # agent/CLI version is a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
  AGENTS_VERSION: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}

jobs:
  sm:
    name: sm / reconcile
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The pack runner resolves .dmtools/config.js from the CWD —
          # the target repo root (machineAuthor, jira.fields, ...).
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve versions (agents release + dmtools CLI)

blocks.text:
# Merge bot factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-merge.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# Why: the SM tick is cron */10 and GitHub cron is BEST-EFFORT — under load
# scheduled runs silently vanish (live: fa ticks stopped for 30+ minutes
# while approved green PRs waited to merge). The merge stage needs no
# orchestration: its evidence (labels + concluded checks + mergeability)
# is fully on the PR. This workflow runs the deterministic, idempotent
# mergeBot.js on EVENTS so conclusions act within seconds:
#
#   workflow_run (the dispatched CI concluded)   — the primary trigger
#   pull_request (labeled / synchronize / edited)— latch-relevant changes
#   check_run (completed)                         — bridge mirrors conclude
#   workflow_dispatch                             — manual / watchdog nudge
#
# The bot performs ONLY: approved+validating+green+CLEAN -> squash-merge
# (one retry on transient refusals, full error surfacing); validating+
# green+CLEAN+unapproved -> latch ai_validated; validating+green+stale
# base -> unarm. Everything else stays SM-owned (no dispatches, no legs).
# Overlap with the SM's merge-validated/validated-green rules is safe:
# both sides are idempotent on the same labels; whoever runs first wins
# and the other becomes a no-op.
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: same as factory-sm.yml — agent code resolves from the
# dmtools-agents RELEASE selected by the caller's vars.AGENTS_VERSION
# ('latest' default), the CLI from vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION. Bumping either is
# a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
#
# Caller stub (machine-merge.yml in the target repo):
#   on:
#     workflow_run: {workflows: ['Quality'], types: [completed]}
#     pull_request: {types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]}
#     check_run: {types: [completed]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {}
#   jobs:

#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@<ref>
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dry-run:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      ci_workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME this repo dispatches on PR heads (fa: ci.yml, dart: quality.yml) — the bot's workflow-run fallback reads its runs when a head carries no check runs (API silent-updated heads, live fa #762)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — GitHub API access for the merge bot (labels, PR state, checks, merge).'
        required: true

# NOTE: NO concurrency block here — deliberately. A called workflow's
# concurrency NEVER applies (GitHub ignores it; only the caller's does),
# and a caller + callee sharing the SAME group name makes every run fail
# at startup with zero jobs and no annotations (live bisect 2026-09-22:
# probes D-G green without it, H red with group name collision, H1 green
# after rename). The caller stub owns the group (machine-merge-bot).

permissions:

  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

env:
  # Version knobs resolve from the CALLER's repository variables (vars.*

  AGENTS_VERSION: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}

jobs:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@b93dc51c1030839153c9bb86c8aa2e6b3fad82de
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 210e8ac5efa06db24a249f174d12f98aadbcb9ab
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @9bea0f9052e877a0dd44149aaaa92d31e114d6c0 — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@b93dc51c1030839153c9bb86c8aa2e6b3fad82de
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@b93dc51c1030839153c9bb86c8aa2e6b3fad82de
    with:
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rewor…

blocks.text:
# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
#       secrets: inherit

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      factory_ref:
        description: 'The dmtools-agents ref the factory runs from (the literal in the stub uses-line). github.workflow_ref cannot serve: in a called workflow it carries the CALLER ref, not the uses-ref.'
        required: true
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" skips — for pure-Dart targets that only need dart from the runner image. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0").'
        required: false
        default: 'stable'
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  # actions/cache@v6 save phase needs actions:write on github.token.
  actions: write

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      config: ${{ steps.check.outputs.config }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
      anchor: ${{ steps.check.outputs.anchor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository (config, runners)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # caller-repo checkout: the factory reads .dmtools/config.js from
          # the TARGET repository, never from the factory pack
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          # Event context rides through from the caller (issues events) —
          # empty for pure dispatches. The guard ALWAYS refreshes from the
          # API (queued runs see a stale payload); this is only a fallback.
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.action || github.event_name }}
          # #544: the `labeled` event sender — the owner-override gate checks
          # its repo permission before honoring a manual agent:rework.
          # Empty for schedule-scan dispatches (SM ticks): the label is
          # trusted as-is there (see rework_override_ok below).

# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home. GitHub requires reusable workflows at the
# .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the callee
# does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing declared one fails
# the guard test (factory_stub_ref_test.dart parity in each caller).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: "PAT for GitHub tool calls + gh CLI (SM engine + validation probes)."
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "Optional dedicated silent-update token; the silent-token input wins when both are set."
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

env:
  # Version knobs resolve from the CALLER's repository variables (vars.*
  # resolve in the caller's context for reusable workflows) — bumping an
  # agent/CLI version is a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
  AGENTS_VERSION: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}

jobs:
  sm:
    name: sm / reconcile
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The pack runner resolves .dmtools/config.js from the CWD —
          # the target repo root (machineAuthor, jira.fields, ...).
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve versions (agents release + dmtools CLI)

# Merge bot factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-merge.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# Why: the SM tick is cron */10 and GitHub cron is BEST-EFFORT — under load
# scheduled runs silently vanish (live: fa ticks stopped for 30+ minutes
# while approved green PRs waited to merge). The merge stage needs no
# orchestration: its evidence (labels + concluded checks + mergeability)
# is fully on the PR. This workflow runs the deterministic, idempotent
# mergeBot.js on EVENTS so conclusions act within seconds:
#
#   workflow_run (the dispatched CI concluded)   — the primary trigger
#   pull_request (labeled / synchronize / edited)— latch-relevant changes
#   check_run (completed)                         — bridge mirrors conclude
#   workflow_dispatch                             — manual / watchdog nudge

# The bot performs ONLY: approved+validating+green+CLEAN -> squash-merge
# (one retry on transient refusals, full error surfacing); validating+
# green+CLEAN+unapproved -> latch ai_validated; validating+green+stale
# base -> unarm. Everything else stays SM-owned (no dispatches, no legs).
# Overlap with the SM's merge-validated/validated-green rules is safe:
# both sides are idempotent on the same labels; whoever runs first wins
# and the other becomes a no-op.
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: same as factory-sm.yml — agent code resolves from the
# dmtools-agents RELEASE selected by the caller's vars.AGENTS_VERSION
# ('latest' default), the CLI from vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION. Bumping either is
# a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
#
# Caller stub (machine-merge.yml in the target repo):
#   on:
